subject: science
prompt_en: Why is the inside of a solar cooker painted black, and why does it have a glass lid and a shiny reflector?
prompt_hi: Solar cooker ka andar ka hissa kaala kyon rang kiya jaata hai, aur usme kaanch ka dhakkan aur chamakdaar reflector kyon hota hai?
answer: Black absorbs as much sunlight as possible; the shiny reflector sends extra sunlight into the box; the glass lid lets sunlight in but traps the warm air so heat is not carried away.

subject: science
prompt_en: Compare two identical houses in Rajasthan, one with a white-painted roof and one with a dark roof. Which stays cooler inside, and why?
prompt_hi: Rajasthan ke do ek jaise gharon ki tulna karo, ek ki chhat safed rang ki aur ek ki gehre rang ki. Kaunsa andar se zyada thanda rahega, aur kyon?
answer: The house with the white roof, because the white surface reflects more sunlight and absorbs less heat.

subject: science
prompt_en: In Ladakh's cold but sunny winters, many people like dark-coloured woollens. Why?
prompt_hi: Ladakh ki thandi par dhoop wali sardiyon mein bahut log gehre rang ke oonee kapde pasand karte hain. Kyon?
answer: Dark colours absorb more sunlight and warm the wearer, and wool traps air that keeps the body's heat in.

subject: science
prompt_en: Why are petrol and oil storage tanks often painted white or silver?
prompt_hi: Petrol aur tel ke bade storage tank aksar safed ya silver rang ke kyon hote hain?
answer: To reflect sunlight and stay cooler, so the fuel inside does not heat up too much and evaporate or build up pressure.

subject: science
prompt_en: Lata writes: 'The Sun heats the air near it, and that hot air travels all the way to Earth.' What is the mistake?
prompt_hi: Lata likhti hai: 'Sun apne paas ki hawa ko garam karta hai, aur wo garam hawa Earth tak aati hai.' Galti kya hai?
answer: Space between the Sun and the Earth is almost empty, with no air to carry heat; the Sun's heat reaches us by radiation, which needs no material.

subject: science
prompt_en: Draw one kitchen scene that shows conduction, convection and radiation, and label each.
prompt_hi: Ek hi kitchen ka scene banao jismein conduction, convection aur radiation teeno dikhen, aur har ek pe label lagao.
answer: Conduction: heat passing through a tawa to a roti, or up a steel spoon in hot dal. Convection: hot water or steam rising in a pot. Radiation: warmth felt on your face standing beside (not over) the stove, or sunlight through the window.

subject: science
prompt_en: Explain to your younger sibling why her white school shirt feels cooler in the sun than her black jacket.
prompt_hi: Apne chhote bhai ya behen ko samjhao ki dhoop mein uski safed school shirt kaali jacket se thandi kyon lagti hai.
answer: The Sun's heat comes as radiation; white cloth reflects most of it while black cloth absorbs most of it and heats up, so the white shirt stays cooler.

subject: science
prompt_en: From last time: which way of heat transfer can work through empty space?
prompt_hi: Pichhli baar se: garmi pahunchne ka kaunsa tareeka khaali space mein bhi kaam karta hai?
answer: Radiation.

subject: science
prompt_en: On a summer evening just after sunset, you stand close to a brick wall that was in the Sun all day. The air is still, yet your face feels warm from the wall. How is heat reaching you?
prompt_hi: Garmi ki shaam, sooraj doobne ke theek baad, tum ek eent ki deewar ke paas khade ho jo din bhar dhoop mein thi. Hawa ruki hui hai, phir bhi deewar se chehre pe garmi lagti hai. Garmi tum tak kaise pahunch rahi hai?
answer: Mostly by radiation: the warm wall, like every warm object (not just the Sun), gives out heat radiation, which travels straight to your face.

subject: science
prompt_en: What is groundwater, and what is the water table?
prompt_hi: Groundwater kya hota hai, aur water table kya hai?
answer: Groundwater is water stored in the tiny gaps in soil, sand, gravel and rock under the ground; the water table is the top level of the layer in which all those gaps are filled with water.

subject: science
prompt_en: Ask an adult to make a few small holes in the bottoms of three plastic cups. Fill one with gravel (small stones), one with sand and one with clay soil. Pour the same amount of water into each. Predict which lets the water through fastest and which slowest.
prompt_hi: Kisi bade se 3 plastic ke cup ki tali mein kuch chhote chhed karwao. Ek mein bajri (chhote patthar), ek mein ret aur ek mein chikni mitti bharo. Har ek mein barabar paani daalo. Guess karo kaun paani sabse jaldi aur kaun sabse dheere nikaalega.
answer: Gravel fastest, then sand, and clay slowest, because bigger gaps between the pieces let water seep through faster.

subject: science
prompt_en: In a clear plastic bottle with its top cut off by an adult, make layers: gravel at the bottom, then sand, then soil. Pour water slowly on top. Predict where the water will collect and what it will look like.
prompt_hi: Ek saaf plastic ki bottle lo jiska upar ka hissa kisi bade ne kaat diya ho, aur usme parat banao: neeche bajri, phir ret, phir mitti. Upar se dheere dheere paani daalo. Guess karo paani kahaan ikattha hoga aur kaisa dikhega.
answer: It seeps down through the soil and sand and collects in the gaps between the stones at the bottom, filling the spaces, like an aquifer; no open lake forms.

subject: science
prompt_en: Two neighbourhoods get the same rain. One has open soil, gardens and trees; the other is fully covered with concrete and roads. Predict where groundwater will be refilled more, and where more water will flood the streets.
prompt_hi: Do mohallon mein ek jaisi baarish hoti hai. Ek mein khuli mitti, bageeche aur ped hain; doosra poora concrete aur sadkon se dhaka hai. Guess karo kahaan groundwater zyada bharega, aur kahaan sadkon pe zyada paani bharega.
answer: The open-soil neighbourhood refills more groundwater because rain soaks in; in the concrete one, rain runs off, floods the streets and very little reaches the groundwater.

subject: science
prompt_en: Why do many borewells go dry in summer?
prompt_hi: Kai borewell garmi mein kyon sookh jaate hain?
answer: There is no rain for months to recharge the groundwater, while people pump out more water for drinking and farming; the water table falls below the bottom of the borewell.

subject: science
prompt_en: Only with an adult beside you, and standing well back (never put your hand or face near the steam): look at a boiling kettle on the stove. Compare the clear gap right at the spout with the white mist a little above it. Which one is like a cloud, and why?
prompt_hi: Sirf kisi bade ke saath, aur door khade hokar (bhaap ke paas haath ya chehra bilkul mat le jaana): stove pe ubalti ketli ko dekho. Tonti ke theek paas ke saaf hisse aur thoda upar wali safed dhundh ki tulna karo. Inmein se baadal jaisa kaun hai, aur kyon?
answer: The white mist is like a cloud: it is made of tiny water droplets that formed when the invisible water vapour cooled and condensed. The clear part right at the spout is water vapour gas, which we cannot see.

subject: science
prompt_en: A school collects rainwater from its roof through pipes into a recharge pit filled with stones and sand. How does this help the school's borewell?
prompt_hi: Ek school apni chhat ka baarish ka paani pipe se patthar aur ret bhare recharge pit mein ikattha karta hai. Isse school ke borewell ko kaise madad milti hai?
answer: Instead of running off, the rainwater seeps through the pit into the ground, adding to the groundwater and raising the water table near the borewell.

subject: science
prompt_en: In parts of Punjab and Rajasthan, farmers now have to drill borewells much deeper than their grandparents' wells. Why might this be?
prompt_hi: Punjab aur Rajasthan ke kuch hisson mein kisaanon ko ab apne daada-pardaada ke kuon se kahin zyada gehre borewell khodne padte hain. Aisa kyon ho sakta hai?
answer: For years more groundwater has been pumped out, for example to irrigate thirsty crops, than rain has put back, so the water table has fallen deeper.

subject: science
prompt_en: Meenu's drawing shows a big blue lake in a cave under her village, labelled 'groundwater'. What would you change?
prompt_hi: Meenu ki drawing mein gaon ke neeche ek gufa mein bada neela taalab dikhaya gaya hai jis pe 'groundwater' likha hai. Tum kya badloge?
answer: Groundwater is mostly water filling the tiny gaps between grains of soil, sand and gravel and the cracks in rocks; she should draw layers of soil and rock with water in their spaces, with the water table as the top of the wet layer.

subject: science
prompt_en: Draw the water cycle as a loop with arrows linking the sea, the Sun, clouds, rain, a river, the soil, groundwater and a tree. Label each arrow with the right process.
prompt_hi: Jal chakra ko ek loop ke roop mein banao jismein teer samudra, Sun, baadal, baarish, nadi, mitti, groundwater aur ek ped ko jodein. Har teer pe sahi prakriya likho.
answer: Evaporation (sea to air), transpiration (tree to air), condensation (vapour to clouds), precipitation (clouds to land), runoff (land to river to sea), infiltration (soil to groundwater), and groundwater seeping into wells and rivers.

subject: science
prompt_en: Explain to your grandmother where the water in her village well comes from, and why the level rises after the monsoon.
prompt_hi: Apni daadi ya naani ko samjhao ki unke gaon ke kuen ka paani kahaan se aata hai, aur monsoon ke baad paani ka level kyon badh jaata hai.
answer: Rain seeps into the soil and fills the gaps in sand and rock underground; the well is dug below the water table, so groundwater seeps into it. The monsoon rain recharges the groundwater and raises the water table, so the well's level rises.

subject: science
prompt_en: From last time: what is it called when rainwater seeps down into the ground?
prompt_hi: Pichhli baar se: jab baarish ka paani zameen mein ris ke neeche jaata hai, use kya kehte hain?
answer: Infiltration.

subject: science
prompt_en: A pendulum completes 20 oscillations in 30 seconds. What is its time period?
prompt_hi: Ek pendulum 30 second mein 20 oscillations poore karta hai. Uska time period kitna hai?
answer: 30 ÷ 20 = 1.5 seconds.

subject: science
prompt_en: Tie a key to a 50 cm thread, hang it from a table edge and time 10 swings. Now tie two keys together on the same length of thread. Predict: will the time for 10 swings be shorter, longer or about the same?
prompt_hi: Ek chaabi ko 50 cm ke dhaage se baandho, mez ke kinaare se latkaao aur 10 jhoolon ka samay naapo. Ab do chaabiyan saath baandh ke wahi lambaai ka dhaaga rakho. Guess karo: 10 jhoolon ka samay kam hoga, zyada hoga ya lagbhag utna hi?
answer: About the same (around 14 seconds for 10 swings), because the bob's mass does not change the time period.

subject: science
prompt_en: Now shorten the thread from 50 cm to 25 cm. Predict: will the pendulum swing faster or slower than before?
prompt_hi: Ab dhaage ko 50 cm se chhota karke 25 cm kar do. Guess karo: pendulum pehle se tez jhoolega ya dheere?
answer: Faster: a shorter pendulum has a shorter time period (about 1 second instead of about 1.4 seconds).

subject: science
prompt_en: Predict: if you start the pendulum with a small pull versus a slightly bigger pull (still a small swing), will the time period change much?
prompt_hi: Guess karo: agar pendulum ko thoda sa kheench ke chhodo ya thoda zyada kheench ke (par abhi bhi chhota jhoola), toh kya time period mein zyada farak aayega?
answer: Hardly at all: for small swings the time period stays nearly the same, because on a bigger swing the bob also moves faster.

subject: science
prompt_en: Why do we time 20 oscillations and divide by 20, instead of timing just one?
prompt_hi: Hum sirf ek oscillation ki jagah 20 oscillations ka samay naap ke 20 se bhaag kyon dete hain?
answer: One swing is too quick to time accurately because of our reaction time in starting and stopping the stopwatch; timing many swings spreads that error over all of them and gives a more accurate result.

subject: science
prompt_en: Compare a sundial and a pendulum clock. What does each depend on, and when would each fail?
prompt_hi: Sundial aur pendulum ghadi ki tulna karo. Har ek kis cheez pe nirbhar hai, aur kab kaam nahi karega?
answer: A sundial depends on the Sun's shadow, so it fails at night and on cloudy days; a pendulum clock depends on steady swings of a fixed length, so it works day and night but must stay still and be adjusted.

subject: science
prompt_en: At the park, there is a long swing and a short swing. If children just sit and let each swing go to and fro by itself, which one goes to and fro more times in a minute?
prompt_hi: Park mein ek lamba jhoola hai aur ek chhota jhoola. Agar bachche bas baith jaayein aur jhoola apne aap aage-peeche ho, toh ek minute mein kaunsa zyada baar aage-peeche jaayega?
answer: The short swing, because a shorter length gives a shorter time period; how heavy each child is does not matter much.

subject: science
prompt_en: An old grandfather clock has started running slow, losing time. Should the pendulum bob be moved up, making the pendulum shorter, or moved down? Explain.
prompt_hi: Ek purani pendulum wali badi ghadi dheere chalne lagi hai, samay peeche ho raha hai. Pendulum ke bob ko upar karna chahiye, yaani pendulum chhota karna, ya neeche? Samjhao.
answer: Move it up to shorten the pendulum; a shorter pendulum has a shorter time period, so it swings faster and the clock runs faster.

subject: science
prompt_en: Akash counted 'one' every time the bob reached the other side. He counted 20 in 15 seconds and wrote the time period as 0.75 s. What is the mistake?
prompt_hi: Akash har baar 'ek' ginta tha jab bob doosri taraf pahunchta tha. Usne 15 second mein 20 gine aur time period 0.75 s likha. Galti kya hai?
answer: He counted half-oscillations: 20 one-way swings are only 10 complete oscillations, so the time period is 15 ÷ 10 = 1.5 s.

subject: science
prompt_en: Here is a table. Thread length 25 cm, 50 cm, 100 cm; time for 10 oscillations 10 s, 14 s, 20 s. Describe in words what the table shows, and find each time period.
prompt_hi: Ye table dekho. Dhaage ki lambaai 25 cm, 50 cm, 100 cm; 10 oscillations ka samay 10 s, 14 s, 20 s. Shabdon mein batao table kya dikhaati hai, aur har ek ka time period nikaalo.
answer: Time periods: 1.0 s, 1.4 s and 2.0 s. The longer the thread, the longer the time period.

subject: science
prompt_en: Explain to a friend what changes a pendulum's time period and what does not, using your key-and-thread experiment.
prompt_hi: Apne chaabi-dhaage wale experiment se dost ko samjhao ki pendulum ka time period kis cheez se badalta hai aur kis se nahi.
answer: Changing the length changes the time period: shorter swings faster, longer swings slower. Changing the mass of the bob (one key or two) does not, and a slightly bigger small swing hardly does either.

subject: science
prompt_en: From last time: what was the giant sundial at Jantar Mantar used for?
prompt_hi: Pichhli baar se: Jantar Mantar ki vishaal sundial kis kaam aati thi?
answer: To tell the time of day from the position of its shadow (it is called the Samrat Yantra).

subject: science
prompt_en: A train covers 240 km in 3 hours. What is its average speed?
prompt_hi: Ek train 3 ghante mein 240 km tay karti hai. Uski average speed kitni hai?

subject: science
prompt_en: Rani walks 600 m in 10 minutes. What is her speed in metres per minute, and in metres per second?
prompt_hi: Rani 10 minute mein 600 m chalti hai. Uski speed metre per minute mein kitni hai, aur metre per second mein kitni?
answer: 600 ÷ 10 = 60 m per minute; 60 m in 60 seconds = 1 m/s.

subject: science
prompt_en: Before calculating, predict who is faster: Ajay, who runs 100 m in 20 s, or Bina, who runs 60 m in 10 s. Then check by calculating.
prompt_hi: Hisaab lagaane se pehle guess karo kaun tez hai: Ajay, jo 100 m 20 second mein daudta hai, ya Bina, jo 60 m 10 second mein daudti hai. Phir hisaab se check karo.
answer: Bina: her speed is 60 ÷ 10 = 6 m/s, while Ajay's is 100 ÷ 20 = 5 m/s.

subject: science
prompt_en: A car's odometer reads 12,500 km before a trip and 12,680 km after. The trip took 3 hours. Predict: must the speedometer have shown 60 km/h the whole time?
prompt_hi: Ek car ka odometer safar se pehle 12,500 km aur baad mein 12,680 km dikhata hai. Safar 3 ghante ka tha. Guess karo: kya speedometer poore samay 60 km/h hi dikhata raha hoga?
answer: No. The average speed was 180 ÷ 3 = 60 km/h, but the speedometer showed different speeds at different moments: slower in traffic, faster on the highway.

subject: science
prompt_en: Two trains leave at the same time for a city 300 km away. Train A's average speed is 100 km/h and train B's is 75 km/h. Predict how much earlier train A arrives, then calculate.
prompt_hi: Do trainein ek hi samay 300 km door ek shehar ke liye chalti hain. Train A ki average speed 100 km/h hai aur train B ki 75 km/h. Guess karo train A kitni pehle pahunchegi, phir hisaab lagao.
answer: Train A takes 300 ÷ 100 = 3 hours and train B takes 300 ÷ 75 = 4 hours, so A arrives 1 hour earlier.

subject: science
prompt_en: Why does a speedometer reading of 50 km/h NOT mean the car has travelled 50 km?
prompt_hi: Speedometer pe 50 km/h dikhne ka matlab ye kyon NAHI hai ki car 50 km chal chuki hai?
answer: It shows how fast the car is going at that moment, meaning it would cover 50 km in one hour at that speed; the distance already travelled is shown by the odometer.

subject: science
prompt_en: Compare: a cheetah sprints 300 m in 12 s; a horse gallops 2 km (2000 m) in 2.5 minutes (150 s). Which moves at the greater speed?
prompt_hi: Tulna karo: ek cheetah 12 second mein 300 m daudta hai; ek ghoda 2.5 minute (150 second) mein 2 km (2000 m) daudta hai. Kiski speed zyada hai?
answer: The cheetah: 300 ÷ 12 = 25 m/s, while the horse's speed is 2000 ÷ 150 ≈ 13.3 m/s.
